extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria in the MPEP governing correspondence addresses, representation (powers of attorney), practitioner status (death/suspension/not_of_record), telephone interviews, and procedures when inventors are dead, incapacitated, or unavailable under 37 CFR and related statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A filing date is granted to a nonprovisional application filed in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office if it includes at least a specification containing a description pursuant to 37 CFR 1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to 37 CFR 1.75, and any drawing referred to in the specification or required by 37 CFR 1.81(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application accorded a filing date does not include the appropriate basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, or oath or declaration, the applicant will be notified and given a period within which to file the missing parts and to pay the surcharge as set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(f) (nonprovisional) or 1.16(g) (provisional) to prevent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for the Office to notify the applicant regarding missing parts or surcharges, a correspondence address must be provided by the applicant; the correspondence address may be different from the post office address of the applicant (e.g., the applicant's registered attorney or agent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to provide a correspondence address, the Office cannot provide notice and the applicant will be considered to have constructive notice as of the filing date that the application must be completed; the applicant will have 2 months from the filing date to do so before abandonment. Periods for completion may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136. Applications not completed timely will be abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office notification and surcharge timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If required fees or an oath/declaration are missing, the Office notifies the applicant and gives a period to file the missing parts and pay the surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f) for nonprovisional; 1.16(g) for provisional) to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not complete filing within the given period (subject to extension under 37 CFR 1.136), the application will be abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence with associate attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Where attorneys bear relation of principal attorney and associate attorney, correspondence will be had with the associate attorney unless the principal attorney directs otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The associate attorney may specify or change the correspondence address to which communications about the application are to be directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two patent practitioners named — indicate correspondence preference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant simultaneously appoints two principal patent practitioners, he or she should indicate with whom correspondence is to be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one is a local Washington metropolitan area practitioner and the applicant fails to indicate either practitioner, correspondence will be conducted with the local practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of later second practitioner without revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after one patent practitioner is appointed, a second is later appointed without revocation of the first practitioner's power, the correspondence address of the second practitioner is entered into the application file record so Office letters are to be sent to him or her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office practice is to send letters to the practitioner whose correspondence address is of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers filed by registered practitioners not of record (37 CFR 1.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers may be filed in patent applications and reexamination proceedings by registered attorneys or agents not of record under 37 CFR 1.34; filing such papers is considered a representation that the attorney or agent is authorized to act in a representative capacity on behalf of applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews with a registered attorney or agent not of record will ordinarily be conducted based only on information and files supplied by that attorney or agent. A paper such as an 'Authorization to Act in a Representative Capacity' (Form PTO/SB/84) may be required to show authority; change of correspondence address or documents granting access may only be signed by an attorney or agent not of record if an executed oath or declaration has not been filed in the application (see 37 CFR 1.33(a) and 1.14(c)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of correspondence address / granting access by non-record practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A change of correspondence address or a document granting access (power to inspect) may only be signed by an attorney or agent who is not of record if an executed oath or declaration has not been filed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.33(a) (correspondence address) and 1.14(c)(4). Use of Form PTO/SB/84 (Authorization to Act in a Representative Capacity) is referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of death of a principal patent practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of a principal patent practitioner will be revoked or terminated by his or her death; such revocation will also terminate the powers of those appointed by him or her. A principal may not appoint a 'substitute' whose power is intended to survive the principal's death; such appointment will not be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notification of the death of the sole principal practitioner is received and the application is up for action, correspondence is held with the applicant or assignee who originally appointed the deceased practitioner. Specific form paragraphs (4.02–4.04) provide standard Office action wording and examiner notes regarding mailing copies to applicant/assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office correspondence when practitioner dies (form paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraphs such as ¶ 4.02, 4.03, and 4.04 to address situations where the attorney/agent of record is deceased and to instruct examiners on mailing and copy procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 4.02: Notice received from practitioner's office — power terminated, new practitioner may be appointed, Office correspondence sent to applicant. ¶ 4.03: Notice from other source — copy mailed to applicant or assignee. ¶ 4.04: Application ready for allowance — Notice of Allowance mailed to office of deceased practitioner in absence of a new power; copy also mailed to applicant or assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney ineffective if practitioner suspended or excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Any power of attorney given to a practitioner who has been suspended or disbarred by the Office is ineffective and does not authorize the person to practice before the Office or to represent applicants or patentees in patent matters (see MPEP § 105).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 4.06, 4.07, and 4.08 should be used where power of attorney is given to an attorney or agent who has been suspended from practice before the Office. The Office does not communicate with suspended or excluded practitioners; where the suspended/excluded practitioner is the only practitioner of record, Office action is mailed to inventor(s) as specified in the form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and signing requirements when practitioner suspended/excluded (form ¶ 4.06–4.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the only practitioner of record is suspended or excluded, Office action is mailed to the inventor (¶ 4.06 for sole inventor) or to the first-named inventor (¶ 4.07 for joint inventors); where some practitioners remain unsuspended, ¶ 4.08 applies describing mailing to unsuspended practitioner and inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of an attorney/agent of record, amendments and other papers must be signed by the inventor, or by assignee(s) where applicable, or by a registered practitioner not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34. Form paragraphs include examiner notes about inserting names/addresses and whether to mail copies to inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone interviews: examiner-initiated preference and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Present Office policy places great emphasis on telephone interviews initiated by the examiner; it is not necessary for a patent practitioner to request a telephone interview, and examiners are not required to note or acknowledge requests or state reasons why proposed interviews would not be considered effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is desirable for a patent practitioner to call the examiner if the call will be beneficial to advance prosecution (see MPEP §§ 713.01 and 713.05). Registered attorneys or agents not of record should not be telephoned for restriction requirements, approval of examiner's amendments, or given any information relative to the patent application by telephone. Non-registered representatives of the practitioner of record should also not be telephoned for such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for placing long-distance telephone calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should place all long distance telephone calls through the FTS (Federal Telecommunications System), even though collect calls may have been authorized by the patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate telephone calls, include complete telephone number (area code and extension) of the person with whom the interview should be held on amendments, letters of transmittal, and powers of attorney, preferably near the signature; telephone number may appear on letter of transmittal or in power of attorney, oath, or declaration next to practitioner's name and address.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO employee inventors and signing oaths
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees of the United States Patent and Trademark Office who were inventors are not permitted to sign an oath or declaration for a patent application during the period of their employment with the Office and one year thereafter (35 U.S.C.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These employees (inventors) will be treated as being unavailable to sign the oath or declaration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.47.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of inventor effects on power of attorney and prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a power of attorney is coupled with an interest (e.g., practitioner is assignee or part-assignee), the death of the inventor (or joint inventor) terminates the power of attorney given by the deceased inventor; a new power from heirs, administrators, executors, or assignees is necessary if the deceased inventor is sole inventor or all powers have been terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives of deceased inventors may make the necessary oath or declaration and apply for and obtain the patent under 35 U.S.C. 117 and 37 CFR 1.42. The Office no longer requires proof of authority of the legal representative, though the representative should ensure proper authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution by administrator or executor (35 U.S.C. 117 / 37 CFR 1.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representatives (executor, administrator, etc.) of deceased or incapacitated inventors may make the necessary oath or declaration, and apply for and obtain the patent on the same terms and conditions applicable to the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One who expects to be appointed legal representative may apply as legal representative in accordance with 37 CFR 1.42. Heirs may act as legal representative where no executor/administrator will be appointed, identifying themselves as such in the oath/declaration submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.64.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executor/administrator discharge and need for new letters
rubrics_metrics.description: When an administrator or executor has performed functions and been discharged and it is desired to make an application for an invention of the deceased, it is necessary for the administrator or executor to take out new letters of administration in order to file a new application for the invention of the deceased inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cures lack of authority after discharge; check jurisdictional requirements for reissuance of letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention of executor not compulsory when inventor dies after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an inventor dies after filing an application and executing the oath or declaration required by 37 CFR 1.63, the executor or administrator should intervene, but allowance of the application will not be withheld nor the application withdrawn from issue if the executor or administrator does not intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor of a pro se application dies after filing, living joint inventors must submit proof that the other is dead; then only living inventors' signatures are required unless legal representative intervenes, in which case signatures of living inventors and legal representative are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.47(a) — filing when at least one joint inventor available
rubrics_metrics.description: If a joint inventor refuses to join in an application or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, the application may be made by the other inventor on behalf of himself or herself and the nonsigning inventor, accompanied by petition and fee as required (37 CFR 1.47(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application deposited under 37 CFR 1.47(a) must meet: (A) all available joint inventors must make oath/declaration on their own behalf (37 CFR 1.63/1.175) and on behalf of the nonsigning inventor (37 CFR 1.64); (B) application must be accompanied by proof that nonsigning inventor cannot be found/reached after diligent effort or refuses to execute papers; (C) last known address of nonsigning inventor must be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.47(b) — filing when no inventor available (filing by person with proprietary interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing under 37 CFR 1.47(b) and 35 U.S.C. 118 is permitted only when no inventor is available; a person to whom the inventor has assigned or agreed in writing to assign, or who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest, may file on behalf of and as agent for the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for 37 CFR 1.47(b) include: (A) the 1.47(b) applicant must make oath required by 1.63/1.64 or 1.175; where corporation files, an officer normally signs or an authorized person signs with proof of authority or statement by corporate officer; (B) the applicant must state his/her relationship to the inventor per 1.64; (C) application must be accompanied by proof that the inventor cannot be found/reached after diligent effort or refuses to execute; (D) last known address of inventor must be stated; (E) applicant must make a prima facie case of assignment or written agreement to assign or otherwise demonstrate proprietary interest; (F) applicant must prove necessity to file to preserve rights or prevent irreparable damage; applicable fee (§ 1.17(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof requirements and limitations for invoking 37 CFR 1.47
rubrics_metrics.description: A bona fide attempt must be made to comply with 37 CFR 1.47 at the time the oath or declaration is first submitted; proof of unavailability/refusal must fully describe exact facts relied upon to establish diligent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the oath/declaration and evidence are not acceptable, the 1.47 applicant will be notified of reasons and may request reconsideration and file supplemental evidence. Temporary unavailability reasons (vacation, being out of town) or hospitalization/non-consciousness are not acceptable reasons for 1.47; 37 CFR 1.43 may apply for incapacity/insanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office processing of 37 CFR 1.47 filings and examiner limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.47 are forwarded by the Office of Initial Patent Examination to the Office of Petitions for a determination whether papers are proper, complete, and acceptable under 37 CFR 1.47 and for a decision on the petition before the application is sent to the Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since an application without an oath or declaration executed by all inventors may be an incomplete application, an examiner should not mail an Office action in an application without a fully executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 unless the application has been accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47 in a written decision on the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of unavailability details (what counts as diligent effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inability to find or reach a nonsigning inventor 'after diligent effort' is the reason for filing under 37 CFR 1.47, a statement of facts should be submitted that fully describes the exact facts relied on to establish that a diligent effort was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts such as vacation, temporary unavailability, or hospitalization/non-consciousness are not acceptable bases for 1.47 filings; in those circumstances, 37 CFR 1.43 may be available instead. Petitions under 1.47 will be dismissed if inappropriate.
